text:
aj: Hey — quick Q on SDK telemetry: what User-Agent do our SDKs send by default, do we honor trace propagation (traceparent/tracestate), and what's the supported way for customers to disable client-side metrics? Need an answer I can paste into a support reply.

maria: Short: our SDKs send a standardized UA string and also set a fallback header (X-Redwood-UA) for environments that strip User-Agent. We honor W3C traceparent/tracestate for incoming requests and will propagate them to the backend when possible. To disable client-side telemetry you can either pass an explicit config flag in the SDK or set an env var.

maria: Example snippets — Node: 
```js
// init with telemetry off and custom UA suffix
const client = new Redwood({
  apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY,
  telemetry: { enabled: false }, // disables client-side metrics/pings
  userAgentSuffix: 'myapp/1.2.3'
});
```

maria: Python: 
```py
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY'), telemetry_enabled=False)
# or set REDWOOD_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 in env
```

maria: Go: 
```go
cfg := redwood.DefaultConfig()
cfg.TelemetryEnabled = false
cfg.UserAgentSuffix = "myapp/1.2.3"
client := redwood.NewClient(cfg)
```

chen: Streaming note: when using streaming endpoints the SDK opens a persistent connection (HTTP/2 or chunked HTTP1). The client reports connection-level metrics (connect time, bytes/sec, chunk counts). If a customer disables client telemetry the SDK stops emitting those local metrics, but server-side telemetry (Redwood's backend) still records request-level metrics for billing/observability unless the customer has an enterprise opt-out. Also: retries + streaming = tricky — if the client re-opens a stream, you may see multiple connect events. :thinking:

oliver: Quick question on traces+retries — if the SDK retries a failed call, does it reuse the same traceparent or create a new one?

maria: By default we try to preserve the same trace context for retries that are part of the same logical request (so you get one logical trace with retry spans). If you want a fresh trace for each attempt you can pass retryKeepTrace=false in config. Example: 
```js
const client = new Redwood({ retry: { attempts: 3, keepTraceOnRetry: true } });
```

aj: How should customers add their own User-Agent? We want to keep our prefix for easier debugging but allow app info.

maria: We recommend using userAgentSuffix / UserAgentAppend option so SDK will send e.g. 
User-Agent: Redwood-Client/node/1.4.0 (+https://example.com) myapp/1.2.3
If they override User-Agent entirely we append a warning during init, because some proxies strip UA and our server-side heuristics rely on the Redwood prefix. You can also set the X-Redwood-UA header manually:
```http
X-Redwood-UA: Redwood-Client/node/1.4.0 myapp/1.2.3
traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01
```

oliver: Are there env var names customers should use for automation?

maria: Yes — common ones: REDWOOD_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 (turns off client-side metrics), REDWOOD_USER_AGENT_SUFFIX, REDWOOD_KEEP_TRACE_ON_RETRY=true. We added those specifically for automated builds/enterprise installs.

devex-bot: Internal doc: https://redwood.internal/devex/telemetry (covers UA format, trace propagation examples, and enterprise opt-out process). :link: 

aj: Perfect — short summary I can paste: "SDKs send a Redwood-prefixed User-Agent (with X-Redwood-UA fallback), we honor W3C traceparent/tracestate and will propagate traces across retries by default, and customers can disable client-side telemetry via SDK config or REDWOOD_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1. Streaming opens persistent connections so disabling client telemetry suppresses local connection metrics but not server-side telemetry." Thanks all. :thumbsup:

maria: Happy to help — ping me if you want a two-line blurb for the public docs.
